To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the basic N-terminal and acidic C-terminal regions of the maize HMGB proteins flanking the HMC-box domain modulate the stimulator function of HMGB proteins for the binding of Dof2 to its DNA target site, and that this modulatory function is different for HMGB1 and 5.
the basic N-terminal and the acidic C-terminal domain flanking the HMO-box domain of HMGB proteins modulate the stimulation of the DNA binding of maize transcription factor Dof1 and Dof2.
the basic and acidic terminal regions flanking the DNA binding HMG-box domain modulate the efficiency of HMGB proteins to stimulate the DNA binding of the plant transcription factor Dof1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a mechanism that allows HMGB proteins to modulate the DNA binding of a transcription factor in a highly efficient manner.

the functional interaction between HMGB proteins and the plant transcription factor Dof1, and it reveals that the terminal domains of HMGB proteins modulate the stimulation of the DNA binding of this transcription factor.
the identification of structural features of HMGB proteins that modulate the stimulationality of Dof2 binding to DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both the acidic and basic regions of HMGB1/2/5 modulate the interaction between HMGB proteins and Dof2, and that these effects are additive.
the C-terminal acidic domains of HMGB proteins are important for the stimulation of the binding of Dof2 to the DNA target site.
the basic N-terminal regions negatively affect Dof2-Dna interaction, whereas the acidic C-terminal regions positively affect this interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the terminal domains of HMGB proteins modulate the interaction of HMG-box domains with Dof2, but that the interaction of HMGB proteins with Dof2 is not determined by the overall DNA binding affinity of HMGB proteins.
HMGB proteins with different structural features can stimulate Dof2-DNAbinding to various degrees.
the acidic C-terminus of HMGB proteins is a key determinant for the stimulation of Doff-DNA binding, whereas the basic N-terminus is less important.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acidic C terminus of HMGB5, which is unique among plant HMGB proteins, is a major determinant of the stimulatory effect of this HMGB on Dof2-DNAbinding.
the basic and acidic domains flanking the HMC-box domain can modulate the interaction of plant HMGB proteins with DNA-binding transcription factors.

HMGB5 and HMGB1 are not simply different variants of HMGB proteins but that the terminal domains of these proteins are functionally specialized to modulate the interaction of HMGB with transcription factors.
